newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market edge mostly lower but call up.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market edge mostly lower but call up.

text.p: Dutch call money edged higher on Tuesday in a fairly active market.
Dealers said call money was most active, quoted at 2.81 to 2.87 percent bid, up some six basis points from Monday.

The other money market rates fell a few basis points. Dealers said this was mainly due to an increasing number of market players factoring in the possibility of a cut in Germany's repo rate in the near future.
"If Germany cuts rates, I see no reason why we shouldn't follow suit," one dealer said, adding that the guilder was strong enough to support another rate cut.

However, in a recent research publication ABN AMRO said the Dutch central bank might not fully match a German repo rate cut in order to reduce the gap between Dutch money market rates and the bank's official rates.
Three-month deposits were down three basis points at 2.91 percent bid, while one-year deposits lost 0.01 at 3.05 percent bid. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
